newsitem.title: USA: Abbott Labs earnings up 11 percent, matching forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Abbott Labs earnings up 11 percent, matching forecasts.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories Inc., the makers of Similac infant formula, Thursday said second-quarter profits rose 11 percent to $522 million, matching Wall Street expectations.
Net income, equivalent to 68 cents a share, compared with $470 million, or 60 cents a share, in the year-ago second quarter.
Total worldwide sales for Abbott were $2.9 billion in the second quarter, up 7.5 percent from a year ago, when the company had sales of $2.7 billion.

Worldwide sales of pharmaceutical and nutritional products reached $1.676 billion on the quarter, up 9.4 percent from a year ago, while worldwide sales of hospital and laboratory products totalled $1.22 billion, up 4.9 percent from the same period last year.

In addition to the milk-based Similac, Abbott makes dozens of other nutritional and health products, including the soy-based infant formula Isomil, the infant oral electrolyte solution Pedialyte and prescription drugs, such as the antibiotic Biaxin and the AIDS drug Norvir.
Abbott is also one of the world's largest manufacturers of hospital and laboratory systems for testing blood.
"Each of Abbott's businesses performed well in the second quarter," said Chairman and Chief Executive Duane Burnham.

On a geographic basis, total quarterly U.S. sales were $1.77 billion, up 9.5 percent. Total non-U.S. sales, including direct exports from the United States, were $1.13 billion, up 4.3 percent from 1996.
The company said a stronger dollar cut into international sales by 7.2 percent.
Abbott's stock fell 6 cents to $66.375 at midday on the New York Stock Exchange.
